title: Everyday Worship
description: General User → Beginner. Familiar worship facts, broader basics and short everyday applications covering prayer, purification, fasting, charity, remembrance and supplication. All questions are Beginner level; detailed disputed rulings and reference-number memorization are excluded.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: How many obligatory daily prayers are there?
questions.explanation: The five daily prayers form a central part of Muslim worship.

questions.question: Which list names the five daily prayers in order?
questions.explanation: The prayers follow the day from dawn through midday, afternoon, sunset and night.

questions.question: Which daily prayer is offered at dawn before sunrise?
questions.explanation: Fajr is the dawn prayer; its time ends at sunrise.

questions.question: Which daily prayer begins at sunset?
questions.explanation: Maghrib is the sunset prayer. Sunset also marks the end of the daily fast.

questions.question: What is wudu?

options.text: The meal that ends a fast

questions.explanation: Wudu is purification that includes washing specified body parts and wiping the head.

questions.question: What direction do Muslims normally face in prayer?
questions.explanation: The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba; its compass direction depends on location.

questions.question: What is the adhan?
questions.explanation: The adhan announces prayer time and calls people to worship.

questions.question: What does the iqamah announce?

options.text: The end of the Friday sermon alone
The immediate start of congregational prayer

questions.explanation: The iqamah is the call given as the congregation prepares to begin prayer.

questions.question: Which opening surah is regularly recited in salah?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah has a central place in the recitation of prayer.

questions.question: What is ruku in salah?
questions.explanation: Ruku is the bowing posture in prayer, performed with calmness.

questions.question: What is sujud in salah?
questions.explanation: Sujud is prostration, one of the postures of prayer.

questions.question: In which month do Muslims observe the obligatory month-long fast?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the month of obligatory fasting for those to whom the duty applies.

questions.question: When does the daily Ramadan fast begin?
questions.explanation: The fast begins at true dawn, when Fajr time begins, rather than at sunrise.

questions.question: What is suhur?
questions.explanation: Suhur is the meal eaten before the fast begins, and the Prophet encouraged it.

questions.question: What is iftar?
questions.explanation: Iftar is the breaking of the fast once sunset has arrived.

questions.question: Which is the prescribed obligatory charity when its conditions are met?
questions.explanation: Zakah is an obligation for those who meet its conditions; it is distinct from voluntary giving.

questions.question: On which day is Jumuah prayer held?
questions.explanation: Jumuah is the weekly Friday congregational prayer.

questions.question: Which act is the pilgrimage to the Sacred House in Makkah?
questions.explanation: Hajj is the pilgrimage associated with the Sacred House, required of those who are able and meet its conditions.

questions.question: What does dhikr mean in worship?
questions.explanation: Dhikr is remembrance of Allah, including words of praise and glorification.

questions.question: What is dua?

options.text: The name of a prayer posture

questions.explanation: Through dua, a person turns to Allah and asks for help and good.

questions.question: What important purpose of salah is stated in the Quran?
questions.explanation: Prayer is worship and a means of remembering Allah.

questions.question: Can the daily prayers simply be moved to any convenient time without a valid reason?

options.text: Yes, every prayer has the same time
Yes, all five are only weekly

questions.explanation: The Quran describes prayer as a duty with appointed times. Specific concessions have their own rules.

questions.question: In wudu, how are the arms washed as specified in the Quran?

options.text: Up to and including the elbows
Only the backs of the hands

questions.explanation: The Quran specifies washing the arms to the elbows as part of wudu.

questions.question: What action is specified for the head in wudu?

options.text: Covering it with dust every time

questions.explanation: Wiping the head is among the acts of wudu described in the Quran.

questions.question: Which action clearly breaks wudu?
questions.explanation: Passing wind breaks wudu, so purification must be renewed before prayer when water can be used.

questions.question: What purification is provided when water cannot be found and its conditions apply?
questions.explanation: Tayammum is purification using clean earth under prescribed conditions. Its method should be learned properly.

questions.question: How should the postures of prayer be performed?

options.text: As a race with other people

questions.explanation: The Prophet taught a man to bow, stand, prostrate and sit with calmness.

questions.question: What practice is encouraged for rows in congregational prayer?
questions.explanation: The Prophet instructed worshippers to straighten their rows.

questions.question: What spiritual aim of fasting is mentioned in the Quran?
questions.explanation: Fasting is prescribed to help believers develop taqwa, or mindfulness of Allah.

questions.question: Does fasting concern behavior as well as avoiding food and drink?

options.text: Yes, lying and wrongdoing must also be avoided
No, lying becomes allowed while fasting

questions.explanation: The Prophet warned against false speech and wrongdoing while fasting. This question concerns conduct, not a ruling that every sin legally breaks the fast.

questions.question: How should suhur be understood?
questions.explanation: The Prophet encouraged suhur. Missing the meal alone does not invalidate a fast.

questions.question: Once sunset is certain, what practice is encouraged?

options.text: Breaking the fast without unnecessary delay

questions.explanation: The Prophet encouraged prompt iftar when its proper time has arrived.

questions.question: What if a fasting person eats or drinks genuinely forgetfully?

options.text: They should stop on remembering and complete the fast
They must keep eating all day
They must assume every later fast is invalid

questions.explanation: The Prophet instructed someone who ate or drank forgetfully to complete the fast.

questions.question: What does the Quran provide for temporary illness or travel during Ramadan?

options.text: A rule that all worship ends permanently
A concession to make up missed fasts later under its rules
Permission to mock those who fast
A rule that missed fasts never need attention

questions.explanation: The verse allows missed days to be made up for illness or travel. Individual circumstances should be discussed with a qualified person.

questions.question: Which group is specifically included among zakah recipients?
questions.explanation: The Quran names the poor and needy among the eligible categories for zakah.

questions.question: What should someone avoid after giving charity?
questions.explanation: The Quran warns against undermining charity through hurtful reminders or injury.

questions.question: Which expression means praise belongs to Allah?
questions.explanation: Alhamdulillah expresses praise of Allah and is among the beloved words of remembrance.

questions.question: Which expression means Allah is the Greatest?
questions.explanation: Allahu Akbar affirms Allah's greatness and is used in remembrance and prayer.

questions.question: Which expression glorifies Allah as free from imperfection?
questions.explanation: Subhanallah glorifies Allah and affirms His perfection.

questions.question: What response to Allah's blessings does the Quran encourage?
questions.explanation: Gratitude recognizes Allah's blessings and should shape how we live.

questions.question: You are planning a busy day. Which approach helps protect the daily prayers?

options.text: Plan breaks within the prayer times
Leave all prayers until bedtime without a valid reason
Assume work removes every prayer duty
Replace every prayer with a calendar note

questions.explanation: Planning around prayer times is a practical way to care for this obligation.

questions.question: You know you passed wind after making wudu, and water is available. What should you do before praying?

options.text: Assume the earlier wudu is unaffected

questions.explanation: Known passing of wind breaks wudu, so it needs to be renewed before prayer.

questions.question: You are in an unfamiliar place and do not know the qibla. What is a sensible first step?

options.text: Always face east wherever you are
Face the nearest door without checking
Use a reliable direction source or ask someone who knows
Choose the direction with the best view

questions.explanation: Making a reasonable effort to identify the qibla helps prepare for prayer.

questions.question: You notice you are rushing through bowing and prostration. What should you change?

options.text: Skip the postures you find slow
Slow down and settle properly in each posture

questions.explanation: The Prophet's teaching emphasizes settled, calm prayer movements.

questions.question: You cannot stand for an obligatory prayer because of illness, but you can sit. How should you pray?

options.text: Abandon prayer solely because you cannot stand
Wait until you can stand even if recovery takes months
Ask someone to pray all your prayers instead

questions.explanation: The Prophet allowed a person unable to stand to pray sitting, with further accommodation if unable to sit.

questions.question: You genuinely forgot a prayer and now remember it. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until the same day next week
Replace it only with a donation

questions.explanation: The Prophet instructed a person who forgot a prayer to perform it on remembering.

questions.question: You are arranging a row before congregational prayer. Which action follows the Prophet's instruction?

options.text: Encourage everyone to face different directions

questions.explanation: Straightening the rows is part of caring for congregational prayer.

questions.question: Your reliable local timetable shows true dawn has begun. What does that mean for today's fast?

options.text: Only the afternoon counts as fasting
The time to abstain from food and drink has begun

questions.explanation: The daily fast begins at true dawn, not sunrise. Use reliable local timing.

questions.question: You are planning for tomorrow's fast. Which meal follows the Prophet's encouragement?

options.text: A breakfast after sunrise while continuing to call it fasting
A meal that replaces all prayers

questions.explanation: Preparing for suhur helps make room for the blessed pre-dawn meal.

questions.question: Sunset has reliably arrived and food or water is ready. Which choice follows the Sunnah?

options.text: Delay only to appear more devout
Break the fast without unnecessary delay
Refuse food because iftar is discouraged

questions.explanation: Prompt iftar at the proper time follows the Prophet's teaching.

questions.question: You accidentally drank water while genuinely forgetting that you were fasting. What should you do once you remember?

options.text: Stop drinking and continue the fast

questions.explanation: Forgetful eating or drinking is treated differently from deliberately breaking a fast.

questions.question: Someone tries to start an argument while you are fasting. Which response follows Prophetic guidance?

options.text: Use the fast as an excuse to threaten them
Start a fight to prove your strength
Avoid fighting and say that you are fasting

questions.explanation: The Prophet taught fasting people to avoid abusive behavior and not join a fight.

questions.question: A friend suggests lying because you are hungry while fasting. What should you do?

options.text: Invent a story to entertain others
Treat hunger as permission for wrongdoing

questions.explanation: Fasting should be accompanied by guarding speech and conduct.

questions.question: You are ready to distribute zakah. What should you check?

options.text: Only how many followers they have
That the recipient fits an eligible category
Only whether they will praise you
Only whether they wear expensive clothes

questions.explanation: Zakah has defined categories of recipients; eligibility should be checked before payment.

questions.question: You helped someone financially. Which action protects their dignity?

options.text: Announce their private difficulties for praise
Avoid shaming them or repeatedly reminding them
Use the gift to insult them later

questions.explanation: Giving should not be followed by hurtful reminders or humiliation.

questions.question: You feel worried and want Allah's help. What act of worship can you turn to?

options.text: Treat worry as a ban on supplication
Wait until you become famous before asking

questions.explanation: Dua is a way to turn to Allah, who hears His servants' supplication.

questions.question: You have a quiet moment during the day. Which action is remembrance of Allah?

options.text: Reflectively recite words of praise to Allah

questions.explanation: Remembering Allah can be part of ordinary daily life, alongside the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: You receive a blessing you hoped for. What response reflects gratitude?

options.text: Thank Allah and use the blessing responsibly

questions.explanation: Thankfulness recognizes Allah's favor and encourages a responsible response.

questions.question: You are unsure how to perform a prayer correctly. What should you do?

options.text: Give up because beginners make mistakes
Learn from a reliable teacher following the Prophet's guidance
Assume learning the prayer is unnecessary

questions.explanation: The Prophet instructed Muslims to pray as he prayed; reliable instruction helps us learn that example.

questions.question: You feel ashamed of past sins and want to return to worship. Which response fits the Quran's message?

options.text: Decide Allah's mercy can never reach you
Continue sinning because repentance has no purpose
Repent and return to Allah with hope

questions.explanation: The Quran calls sinners not to despair of Allah's mercy. Turn back sincerely rather than abandoning hope.
